Chapter Notes

I fell in love with this AU so I had to write more. This one isn’t as angst-free as the previous part, but it’s really light. Like it’s just flavoring to make the fluff even fluffier.
Also I apologize if there’s differences between my fic and the in game lore of stuff, I have a horrible memory and the hsr wiki isn’t being really helpful.
I hope you enjoy the fic!

See the end of the chapter for more notes

“Welcome home, Mydeimos. I trust your trip to... Aedes Elysiae was worthwhile,” Krateros said, standing at the door to the queen’s office.

Mydei had barely set foot back in Castrum Kremnos before he requested an urgent audience with his mother. Gorgo, ever attentive, had cleared her schedule the moment she received word.

She now sat at her desk, papers stacked to the side, waiting as her son approached.

Mydei walked in, taking a moment to greet her. “Mother,” he said, bowing his head slightly. “Thank you for seeing me.”

Krateros, stood at the door, arms crossed. He had a feeling he knew what this was going to be about.

“What’s so urgent, Mydei?” Gorgo asked.

Mydei didn’t hesitate.

“I want to get married to Phainon.”

Gorgo’s brows lifted, surprise showing across her face, but it vanished almost instantly. She had expected this, though perhaps not so soon.

Krateros, however, was not as composed.

“Mydeimos, you cannot possibly be serious about marrying that country boy!” he exclaimed.

“But Krateros, I love him.” Mydei said firmly.

“That boy is unfit to be your husband.” Krateros replied, pinching the bridge of his nose. He turned to Gorgo, seeking backup.

But the queen remained composed, a faint smile on her face. “I haven’t met him yet,” she said, “but if Mydei believes he’s the right one, then I have no objection.”

Krateros looked between the two royals, thoroughly exasperated. He’s getting too old for this.

“With all due respect, he’s not fit to rule by the prince’s side.”

“He’s my equal,” Mydei shot back, arms crossing over his chest. “He’s proven it to me countless times. It could only ever be him.”

“There will be others, far more suitable for the role,” Krateros insisted, his tone almost desperate.

“It’s too late,” Mydei said.

Krateros narrowed his eyes. “Too late?”

“I’ve already placed my trust in him,” Mydei replied.

A heavy silence fell over the room. Both Gorgo and Krateros understood what those words meant. Mydei had revealed to Phainon the one thing no one else knew, his weak spot, the only way to kill him. Not even they had been entrusted with that secret.

Krateros took a sharp breath, irritated. “You told him?”

Mydei held eye contact, not backing down. “Yes. I trust him with my life.”

Krateros turned away, dragging a hand down his face. “You barely know him.”

“I know enough. More than enough.” Mydei’s tone was final. He rarely stood against Krateros’ advices.

For a moment, Krateros looked like he might argue again, but then he caught sight of Gorgo, watching her son with a look close to pride.

He exhaled, defeated. “Fine. It’s your life to risk.”

With that, Krateros left the room, muttering to himself.

As soon as the door shut behind him, Gorgo chuckled. “Forgive him, Mydei. He’s only protective. He’s watched over you since the day you were born.”

“I know,” Mydei said, his expression softening for a moment. “But I’m serious about marrying Phainon.”

“I can see that,” Gorgo replied, her smile returning. “I’ll clear some time in my schedule to meet him properly. Then, if all goes well, we can begin the wedding preparations.”

Mydei let out a breath he hadn’t realized he was holding, the tension in his shoulders easing. “Thank you.”

Gorgo rose from her desk and crossed the room to him, placing a hand on his arm. “You’ve grown so much, my son.”

She could still picture him as a little boy, curled up in her lap as she read him stories, or trailing behind her during training sessions, declaring that he wanted to be just like her someday. A part of her longed to scoop him into her arms again, something she could probably still do, though it wouldn’t be the same. Her son was old enough to marry now, and she couldn’t be prouder.

“…and then she was telling him embarrassing stories about me! Again!” Phainon complained as he ground the herbs Perdikkas had handed him.

“Hm.” Perdikkas hummed, clearly having checked out of Phainon’s rambling. Ever since he came back from his little honeymoon with Mydei, Phainon hadn’t stopped talking about the trip.

“You’re not listening…”

“I am,” Perdikkas replied, not looking up from the jars he was organizing.

“By the way, I brought you herbs from Aedes Elysiae.”

That snapped Perdikkas’ attention. He turned to look immediately. “You did?”

“I figured you’d be interested,” Phainon said smugly, pulling a wrapped pouch from his bag and handing it over.

Perdikkas took the bundle, untied it, and his eyes lit up. “These are…” He held one of the leaves close to his face to smell it. “This is high quality.”

“They grow in the wild all around Aedes Elysiae,” Phainon said, pleased with himself.

“I might have to visit, if that’s the case.” He began sorting the herbs into labeled jars, the quiet between them stretching just long enough to feel intentional, until Perdikkas broke it.

“So…” he said, not looking up. “Aside from collecting herbs and getting bullied by Cyrene, how did things progress with Mydei?”

Phainon leaned back against the counter, a smile appearing on his face. “It progressed well.”

“That smile says more than ‘well’.”

Phainon rolled his eyes. “Fine. We’re together. Officially boyfriends. Or… whatever term you guys use in Castrum Kremnos.”

Perdikkas paused, raising a brow. “Did he propose to you already?”

Phainon flushed. “Not exactly. But... marriage did come up.”

“Oh?” Perdikkas looked amused now.

Phainon groaned. “Don’t start. That’s Leonnius’ job.”

“I wasn’t going to say anything,” Perdikkas chuckled. “I’m just surprised it took this long.”

“Stop teasing me!”

“You’re in love,” Perdikkas replied. “It’s cute.”

Phainon groaned, letting the silence sit for a moment before speaking again. “You know, I was thinking.”

“That’s unusual.”

“I’ll pretend I didn’t hear that.” Phainon shot him a glare. “I want to learn to speak Kremnoan.”

Perdikkas blinked, finally giving him his full attention. “Seriously?”

“Is it that shocking?”

“A little, yeah. I mean… no one really speaks it anymore. It’s pretty outdated, missing half the words you’d need in a normal conversation. Our generation barely learned the basics, and we never use it.”

“I know,” Phainon said, leaning against the table. “But when we were in Aedes Elysiae, Mydei kept talking about history, how the old language is fading away. I could tell it meant a lot to him. So… I figured I’d learn it. I think it’d make him happy.”

Perdikkas nodded. “That’s… actually pretty thoughtful of you.”

Phainon smirked. “I can be romantic when I want to.”

“Will Mydei be the one to teach you?”

Phainon shook his head. “No. I want to keep it a secret. That’s why I was going to ask you if you could help me.”

Perdikkas frowned. “Unfortunately, I’m not the best person for that. I only learned the basics and then continued my studies of medicine in the common language.”

Phainon slumped a bit, disappointed. “Oh…”

“But,” Perdikkas added after thinking, “I know someone who can help. I’ll talk to him.”

Which was how Phainon found himself in the library of Castrum Kremnos, standing awkwardly across from Ptolemy. They only knew of each other through Mydei, and that one incredibly unfortunate time Ptolemy had walked in on them making out in this very library.

“You want to learn the Kremnoan language?” Ptolemy asked, his tone skeptical, as if he couldn’t quite believe Phainon was serious.

“I do,” Phainon replied.

“And why, exactly? If it’s just to impress Mydei, I’d advise you reconsider.”

“It’s not just for show,” Phainon said. “I know how much Mydei loves history, and I want to share that with him. Speak the language of his land. I know it won’t be easy, and it’ll probably take years, but… I’ve got a lifetime ahead of me.”

Ptolemy was taken aback. That was far more sincere and romantic than he’d expected.

“…Very well,” he said. “But don’t expect me to go easy on you.”

Phainon was led into a secluded wing of the library, a part he had never visited before. After stepping through a wooden door, they entered a room that looked much older than the rest of the library, though still impressively large. The air was dusty, and the books looked like they might crumble at the touch.

As they passed the shelves, Phainon noticed he couldn’t read any of the titles on the spines. The letters were unfamiliar. It must be Kremnoan.

“This is the ancient library,” Ptolemy explained. “The new one was built adjacent to it, but all the old Kremnoan texts were kept here.”

Ptolemy gathered a stack of papers, a few pens, and a thick dictionary bound in worn leather. For the next two hours, they remained holed up in the room. Ptolemy was fluent in Kremnoan, and apparently, Mydei was too. They began with the basics, the shapes of the letters and how each one was pronounced.

By the end of their session, Phainon was tired but insisted he could keep going. But Ptolemy shook his head. “Start by learning these by heart over the next two days. We can add more letters next time.”

Phainon walked out of the library, gazing out the window. The moon hung high in the sky, stars shining in the dark. It was already late, he should be heading to bed soon. Just not his bed.

Mydei’s bed.

The thought made him giddy all over again, remembering their earlier conversation.

“You want me to sleep in your room tonight?” Phainon had asked, trying, and failing to sound casual.

“Is that so strange? We shared a bed in Aedes Elysiae,” Mydei had pointed out.

And really, who was Phainon to argue with a prince?

Now that he thought about it, they’d actually have a proper spacious bed here, unlike the disaster of a mattress they’d shared back in Aedes Elysiae. On the first night, Phainon had offered for Mydei to sleep on top of him since the bed was too small to fit them both.

A decision he immediately regretted once Mydei’s muscular weight settled over him like a boulder. Before Phainon could even wheeze out a complaint about not being able to breathe, the entire bed had collapsed under them. They ended up sleeping on the floor that night

They spent half the next day fixing and making the bed bigger. But that night, when Mydei was in a particularly affectionate mood, they quickly realized another issue. The bed creaked loudly and the walls of the house were thin.

Tonight, they’d have thick walls, a comfortable mattress, and plenty of space. Phainon could hardly wait. He practically skipped down the corridor toward his boyfriend’s room, until he noticed someone standing ahead.

Though they had never met, Phainon recognized her instantly.

She was very tall, and even through the long sleeves of her dress, he could tell she had impressive muscles. Her hair was tied in a long blonde braid that hung over her shoulder, the ends turning red. In the dim corridor light, he couldn’t quite make out the color of her eyes, but the soft wrinkles around them gave away her age.

Phainon was convinced the king’s genes hadn’t even tried, because Mydei was the spitting image of the woman standing in front of him.

He soon realized he’d been staring for a good minute, so he bowed his head slightly in greeting.

“You must be Phainon,” she said. Her voice was deep yet soft, not nearly as intimidating as he’d imagined.

“I am,” he replied, trying to sound composed. So this is what it feels like to be suddenly face to face with royalty. Maybe he owed his parents an apology for neglecting to mention that Mydei was a prince.

“Enough with the formalities,” she said, waving a hand. “You’re my soon to be son in law after all.”

Oh. She knows?

The look on Phainon’s face must have betrayed his surprise, because she added, “I’ve heard a lot about you from my son and others.”

“Mydei has told me a lot about you, too,” Phainon replied, then added quickly, “All good things. He cares about you deeply.”

She smiled at that, pleased with his response.

“He cares a lot about you as well,” she said. “But not everyone is thrilled about your relationship. There are those who say you can’t be trusted.”

Phainon had expected as much, but hearing it still stung. “I figured as much,” he admitted.

“It might be intimidating, being my son’s equal, but I hope that won’t be enough to deter you from standing beside him.”

“Of course not!” Phainon said. “I plan to stay by his side, no matter what.”

Gorgo nodded, satisfied with his conviction. “Good. I heard he revealed to you his weak spot.”

Phainon was surprised with how much the queen knew about his relationship with her son.

“He never told me where it is,” she added. “He says he doesn’t want to burden me with his fate. He believes I’ve carried enough for one lifetime.”

There was a quiet pause, then she continued, “He worries he might turn out like his father. But I know they’re nothing alike. And I hope you can help him see that, especially in moments when he doubts himself.”

“I’ll remind him as many times as he needs,” Phainon said, more serious now. “He wanted me to know his weakness to stop him if ever needed. But I never plan on using it against him. I want to fight side by side with him, and protect him.”

Gorgo smiled softly. “I’m glad Mydei found you.”

Phainon wasn’t sure what to say to that. His throat felt tight, so he simply nodded and offered a smile in return.

“Go now. He’s waiting for you.” She said, and Phainon wasn’t sure he wanted to know how she knew where he was going.

“It was nice meeting you,” he mumbled before heading off.

When he reached Mydei’s room, he opened the door to find his boyfriend bundled up in a thick blanket, his back to the door. Was he asleep?

“Took you long enough…” Mydei’s voice sounded irritated. So, not asleep.

“I’m sorry… I got held up,” Phainon said. He wasn’t sure whether to mention his run-in with Gorgo, and he definitely wasn’t going to bring up the study session with Ptolemy. “Are you mad?”

“No.” Of course he was mad. He had spent nearly an hour waiting, dressed in a loose robe, posed uncomfortably on the bed in what he thought would be a tempting position so Phainon would have a perfect view the second he walked in. But when the door didn’t open, and the minutes dragged on, he’d grown annoyed, changed into sleep clothes, and decided to sulk instead.

“Well, I’m here now.” Phainon sat behind Mydei, wrapping his arms around his torso, seeking to touch his chest. He kissed the side of Mydei’s neck, intending to follow up with another as an apology.

But Mydei pushed him off with a shrug of his shoulder, still pouting into the pillow. “I’m not in the mood anymore.”

“Oh. Would you like to cuddle instead?” Phainon offered. If Mydei didn’t want to do more, he wasn’t going to push.

But Mydei had forgotten just how cute and irresistible his boyfriend could be. It was hard to keep sulking when Phainon was being so sweet and respectful.

He let out a sigh before finally rolling over to face Phainon. “Fine,” he muttered, but the way his arms slid around Phainon’s waist betrayed the fact that he’d already forgiven him. He pulled him close, burying his face in Phainon’s chest.

He closed his eyes, settling in comfortably as Phainon left pecks on his temple.

“Wake me up tomorrow… in a special way.” Mydei said

Phainon’s head lifted. “Special how?”

But Mydei didn’t answer. He’d already shut his eyes and slipped into a very unconvincing act of sleep. He wanted Phainon to get creative. Unfortunately for him, he seemed to forget that Phainon was a complete virgin whose only real experience consisted of making out. With him.

That request stayed in Phainon’s mind all night, keeping him wide awake as far too many ideas tumbled through his head. He needed something Mydei would like. But that was tricky, considering Mydei already hated waking up early. How could he manage it without his boyfriend getting cranky?

By morning, Phainon had barely slept. He got up early, heading to the bathroom to freshen up before putting his plan into action. He knew Mydei liked to sleep in, so timing was important.

When he returned to bed, Mydei had already stolen his pillow and was hugging it, face buried in it. Phainon settled behind him and began pressing soft kisses to his shoulder, slowly working his way up to his neck, then to the shell of his ear.

“It’s time to wake up, love,” he whispered, his voice low as his fingers gently traced and scratched along the skin of Mydei’s back.

His boyfriend stirred at that, but instead of turning toward him, he burrowed his face deeper into the pillow.

“Hmm…”

“What?” Phainon asked.

“I forgot how innocent you are…” Mydei said, his voice clearer now.

“Is that not what you meant by special?” Phainon was confused.

Mydei stretched, letting out a yawn as he shifted away from him. “No, not really.”

“Oh…” Phainon’s disappointment was obvious, his shoulders sinking. He’d really hoped to make up for yesterday’s mistake this morning.

He was so caught up in his own thoughts, he didn’t notice Mydei moving. Before he knew it, his boyfriend was kneeling at the foot of the bed, slipping between his legs and parting them with his arms as he settled in.

“Will you let me show you?” he asked.

Oh. Oh.

So that’s what he meant by special.

Phainon didn’t trust his voice, so he only nodded. Mydei brushed a few loose strands of hair behind his ear before tugging at the waistband of Phainon’s shorts.

Later that morning, they both found themselves in the kitchen, making their own food since they’d missed breakfast. Well, it was more like Mydei cooked while Phainon watched, still a little dazed from the morning’s earlier events.

Phainon leaned against the counter, his eyes following Mydei’s every movement. The marks he had left on the other’s neck were fading already, courtesy of the curse of immortality. What a shame, he really liked the idea of the prince, who always walked around half-naked, showing off his marks.

What Gorgo said the previous day bothered him. “Not everyone is thrilled about your relationship.”

Phainon wasn’t usually the possessive type, but he desperately wanted to prove these people wrong.

His thoughts broke when Mydei set a plate of fresh honeycakes in front of him, the scent reminding him of how hungry he was.

“What are you thinking about?” Mydei asked, curious.

Phainon hesitated, debating between the truth and something lighter.

“You.” he said, his gaze lingered on Mydei a bit too long, focusing on his neck.

Mydei’s cheeks flushed as he stepped closer. “You’re insatiable.”

“That’s not what I meant,” Phainon chuckled, lifting a hand to trace a fading bruise. “I just wish these would last longer.”

“The curse has its perks. You’d hate it if I was covered in marks all the time.”

“I’d love it,” Phainon said, voice low. “My marks suit you.”

Mydei shook his head, smiling despite himself. “Again. You’re insatiable.”  

Before Phainon could answer, Mydei leaned in and captured his lips in a gentle kiss. When he pulled back, Phainon almost chased after his lips.

“We should eat now if we want to get any training done today.”

Weeks passed since that day, since their return to Castrum Kremnos, but little had changed. The only noticeable difference was how inseparable Mydei and Phainon had become. They slept in Mydei’s room, sparred together each morning, and shared every meal with Mydei’s generals. Phainon was already close to Perdikkas and Leonnius, his friendship with Ptolemy steadily growing, and even Peucesta and Hephaestion were beginning to warm up to him.

Afternoons were the only time they spent apart. Mydei attending to whatever princely duties he had, while Phainon assisted Perdikkas in the infirmary and practiced Kremnoan with Ptolemy.

Speaking of Kremnoan, Phainon had already mastered the basics. He could read and write all the letters, recognize simple words, and understand short phrases. His vocabulary and sentence building still needed work, but he was getting the hang of it quickly.

One night, as Phainon laid in bed, Mydei joined him, unusually quiet. Without a word, he sank against Phainon’s chest, exhaling as though something heavy was weighing him down.

“Everything alright?” Phainon asked. By now, he knew his boyfriend had a habit of bottling things up.

“Tomorrow, I’m going to the Sea of Souls,” Mydei said.

Phainon frowned. He knew what the Sea of Souls was, and that it wasn’t a place to go to for fun. “What for?”

“My mother’s signet ring,” Mydei explained. “It once served as a symbol of kingship, though it doesn’t anymore. She meant to pass it down to me, but it was lost in the Sea of Souls. We’ve been trying to locate it for years, and we think we finally know where it is. Tomorrow, Hephaestion, Leonnius, Peucesta, and I will attempt to retrieve it.”

Phainon hummed quietly, letting his fingers trace lines down Mydei’s spine, a small gesture he’d learned helped calm him during stressful moments.

“Can I come with you?” he asked.

“I’d rather you stayed here,” Mydei replied. “I’ve asked Perdikkas and Ptolemy to remain as well. I need people I trust to be here in case something happens while I’m gone.”

Phainon understood the reasoning, but that didn’t make it easier to accept. “Promise me you’ll be careful,” he murmured, pressing his lips to Mydei’s forehead.

“I will,” Mydei said, as Phainon held him just a little tighter.

When Phainon woke the next morning, Mydei was already gone, his side of the bed long cold.

They hadn’t spent more than a few hours apart in weeks. Ever since their trip to Aedes Elysiae, they had been almost inseparable.

“You look like a sad puppy,” Perdikkas remarked over lunch.

With most of the generals away, it was just Ptolemy, Perdikkas, and Phainon sharing a meal outside the infirmary. The big table felt unnecessary, and this spot made it easier to talk freely, and, in Perdikkas’ case, pry for gossip.

“You’re so dramatic,” Ptolemy added with a chuckle. “It hasn’t even been a full day and you’re already sulking.”

“Don’t laugh at me…” Phainon muttered, though his tone lacked any real bite.

“I’m going to laugh at you,” Perdikkas said without hesitation. “Your boyfriend is immortal, in case you’ve forgotten. What are you so worried about?”

“He’s not exactly immortal,” Phainon corrected. “He explained it to me. He can die, but he comes back. That doesn’t make it any less dangerous.” The thought alone made his heart ache. Just because Mydei would return alive didn’t erase the countless deaths he might endure in the process. “And the others aren’t immortal. Aren’t you worried about them?”

“Yeah, Perdikkas,” Ptolemy said, smirking. “Aren’t you worried about Leonnius?”

The sudden pink on Perdikkas’ cheeks told Phainon he was missing some important context.

“No,” Perdikkas said far too quickly. He cleared his throat, composing himself. “They’ve faced worse. They’ll be fine.”

Before Phainon could press him on whatever it was Ptolemy seemed to know, Perdikkas changed the subject. “You know, you should be excited about Mydei going after that ring.”

“Why?”

“He’s probably going to give it to you.” Ptolemy said.

“What? Why me?”

Both of the generals looked at him with deadpan expressions.

“You’re seriously asking?” Perdikkas asked. “He’s going to ask you to marry him.”

The gears finally clicked in Phainon’s mind, and his cheeks flushed bright red.

“I knew he wants us to get married, but does it have to be with this ring?”

“You, of all people, should know how fond Mydei is of history,” Ptolemy said. “The ring may have lost its old symbolism, but my guess is he wants to give it a new meaning, one that belongs to you both.”

Phainon swallowed, the thought making his heart beat faster.

“You have to teach me how to say something romantic in Kremnoan by the time he comes back,” Phainon said, determined to answer the proposal in Mydei’s language.

Both men laughed, clearly amused by his resolve.

“Of course. Now finish eating so we can get to work,” Ptolemy said with a smile.

Chapter End Notes

Chapter Notes

I’m sorry it took so long to upload! The ao3 curse is back at it again. I burned my dominant hand with boiling water and I couldn’t type anything for a few days. But now I’m all good!
Warning: Words said in Kremnoan will be written in bold. I will mention when Kremnoan is used but this will make it easier to distinguish between languages.
Enjoy!

See the end of the chapter for more notes

Phainon spent his days helping in the infirmary and practicing Kremnoan. As for training, he soon discovered that Perdikkas and Ptolemy were far more skilled than he’d realized.

“Of course we can fight. Do you think Mydei made us his generals just for show?” Perdikkas asked.

Not exactly. He had assumed Mydei chose them because they were knowledgeable, and admittedly attractive. Apparently being handsome was a requirement, but he hadn’t realized combat skill was too.

“We all trained with Mydei when we were younger,” Ptolemy explained. “Our studies did differ at some point though.”

From what Phainon gathered, all the generals were capable fighters. Leonnius trained new recruits, while daily drills for Kremnoans were usually led by Hephaestion and Peucesta, with Ptolemy stepping in on occasion. Perdikkas oversaw the injured and recovery.

Sparring against Perdikkas proved insightful. He had a sharp eye for weaknesses and struck at blind spots mercilessly, forcing Phainon to sharpen his reflexes.

Still, it had been a week since Mydei and the others had left, and Phainon was starting to worry. He knew the journey would take time, but he couldn’t help but feel uneasy.

“That’s disgusting. Are we really going to eat that?” Leonnius asked, grimacing as Hephaestion cut pieces of flesh from the monster they had just killed. Mydei crouched nearby, trying to cook it with their limited supplies.

“We don’t have a choice,” Hephaestion replied. “Our rations are low, and the journey’s far from over.”

“As long as Mydei’s the one cooking, I’m sure even the nastiest monster will taste good,” Peucesta said.

Normally, Mydei would have laughed, saying back a line about how every warrior should know how to cook a basic meal. This time, though, he remained quiet.

While Leonnius and Peucesta continued their banter, Hephaestion took the chance to pry.

“Something’s bothering you.”

“No,” Mydei replied too quickly.

“Wrong tone,” Hephaestion said. “That wasn’t a question. I know something’s bothering you.”

Mydei sighed. “It’s been a week since we started this search.”

“And we’re not finished,” Hephaestion reminded him.

“But we’ve checked five of the six possible locations,” Mydei said.

Hephaestion rested a hand on his back, giving it a reassuring pat. “Then it has to be in the sixth. Don’t lose hope just yet.”

“You’re right…” Mydei exhaled, pulling a skewer from the fire to test if it was done cooking. “I just… I really want to give Phainon that ring.”

“You’re smitten,” Hephaestion chuckled.

Before Mydei could reply, Leonnius and Peucesta returned, asking if the food was ready.

After dinner, Mydei and Leonnius agreed to take the first night watch. Later, they would wake Peucesta to relieve one of them. Hephaestion was required to sleep through the night because of his lingering health issues. He had protested often enough, until Perdikkas gave him a stern lecture that ended the argument for good.

Later that night, Hephaestion and Peucesta were fast asleep. Leonnius, on the other hand, was struggling to keep his eyes open. He scooted closer to Mydei and poked his arm.

“Mydei… distract me, please… my eyes are closing on their own…”

“Do I have to remind you that you volunteered to take the first watch?” Mydei whispered back.

“I did, but you’re too quiet. Help me out here.”

Leonnius was always talkative, and conversation would help keep him awake. Maybe humoring him would distract Mydei from the worries sitting at the back of his mind.

“Fine. What do you want to talk about?”

Leonnius grinned. “How are you going to propose to Phainon?”

So that’s what this is about.

“Propose?” Mydei raised a brow. “He already knows we’re getting married. I’m just going to give him the ring.”

“Lame!” Leonnius complained.

Mydei gave him a puzzled look. “What would you suggest, then?”

“Put the ring in his food so he finds it during a romantic candlelit dinner! Or, better, give it to him right after you beat him in a spar!” Leonnius listed off.

“Wow,” Mydei smirked. “Sounds like someone’s been fantasizing about their own proposal.”

“What? Me? Pfft… don’t be ridiculous.” Leonnius turned away too quickly, and even in the dim light Mydei caught the flush creeping across his cheeks.

Mydei let the silence hang for a moment, just long enough to make Leonnius fidget. Then he spoke up again.  “So… would you prefer the candlelight dinner proposal, or the sparring match?”

Leonnius whipped his head around. “I told you, I wasn’t talking about me!”

“Mm.” Mydei hummed. “Because if it were about you, I’d have to ask who exactly are you picturing receiving that ring?”

Leonnius laughed nervously instead of answering, knowing his voice would come out cracked.

Mydei smirked. “Don’t worry. Your secret is safe with me.”

“I don’t have a secret,” Leonnius said, crossing his arms over his chest.

“Of course not,” Mydei said, leaning back into his spot. “But I have to warn you that Perdikkas isn’t really fond of sweating. He’d enjoy a dinner more.”

Leonnius was about to protest, but he sank in his spot. “I know that…” he mumbled.

Mydei smiled faintly, but didn’t press further. Before long, Leonnius’ head tilted to the side as he fell asleep. Mydei noticed Peucesta still fast asleep. He already knew he wouldn’t get any sleep tonight, so he might as well let the others rest while they could.

The next day, once everyone was properly awake, they set off toward the sixth location. As expected, their path was filled with monsters. By now, they knew what they had to do. Fight off the monsters, clear the area, then search.

But as they drew closer to the sixth location, the attacks ceased. Not a single creature crossed their path.

“Something’s not right,” Hephaestion pointed out.

“Stay alert,” Mydei warned, scanning the area. Weak monsters only avoided places where something far stronger resided.

The land beneath their feet kept thinning as they pressed on, forcing them to walk in a single line. Mydei took the lead, ready to tank whatever waited for them.

“Wait!” Leonnius suddenly called from the rear. “There’s something gold shining inside the river!”

The others turned their heads, but the water was too restless to reveal what hid beneath its surface. The ripples seemed unnatural.

“Let’s not get hasty,” Peucesta cautioned. “We can search properly once we’re sure it’s safe.”

“I can probably reach it with a branch! It’s so close, and it could be the signet ring!” Leonnius said, snatching up a fallen branch and dipping it into the water.

Mydei was maybe too hopeful, a fatal mistake. His attention shifted toward Leonnius and the glint beneath the current. That single moment of distraction cost them. No one noticed the trail of bubbles surging to the surface until it was too late.

“Leonnius, move!” Hephaestion shouted in panic, realizing the movement a little too late.

The river exploded. A massive beast erupted from the water, jaw opening wide enough to swallow a man whole. It lunged straight at Leonnius, mouth wide open.

But Leonnius barely had time to look up before the attack hit.

Phainon was in his room, bent over the notebook where he copied down the new sentences Ptolemy had taught him. It was the only place he could keep them hidden from Mydei.

But then, he heard noises outside. He set his pen aside, and crossed to the window. His heart skipped when he saw Mydei and the others returning. They were back, finally! But far too many people had gathered around them and Phainon couldn’t see them properly.

He bolted from his room, leaping down the stairs two, sometimes three at a time, nearly tripping in his rush. It didn’t matter, nobody was paying attention.

He ran across the path that led past Perdikkas’ infirmary, but that’s when he saw Hephaestion and Peucesta carrying Leonnius inside. Leonnius was limp in their arms, drenched in blood.

Phainon froze in place. What happened out there?

Before he could follow them in, he saw Mydei approaching from the corner of his eye.

“Phainon…” Mydei’s voice was low, his eyes refusing to meet Phainon’s. He looked pained, almost guilty. His armor and skin covered with red blood, and Phainon could only assume most of it belonged to Leonnius.

“Mydei, what happened?” Phainon asked, stepping closer.

Mydei shook his head. “Not here,” he said, glancing around. Too many eyes were on them, and the prince never liked looking vulnerable, especially not in front of his people.

“Let’s go to the baths,” Phainon blurted out. The suggestion startled Mydei enough to pull him out of his daze. “So we can wash the blood off… and then we can talk.”

Mydei finally seemed to understand, so he nodded. He led Phainon toward his private baths. Normally, the space was shared between Mydei and his generals, but with most of them occupied, the two of them would have some privacy.

Both of them undressed in silence, the only sound being Mydei’s armor hitting the ground. Phainon led him into the bath, taking a washcloth with him to scrub him once Mydei settled into the hot water. Mydei let out a groan, finally resting his forehead against his boyfriend’s shoulder.

Phainon didn’t speak, he knew Mydei needed time to rearrange his thoughts. Instead, he grazed his fingers gently along the back of his neck, tracing slowly down his spine in a soothing rhythm.

Little by little, Mydei seemed to melt into his arms.

“I messed up…” he admitted at last. “I thought Leonnius had found the ring. I was so focused on it that I didn’t notice the monster approaching. He barely avoided the worst of it, but it got his leg… and he lost so much blood…”

Phainon pulled him closer, whispering, “Perdikkas will patch him up… he’ll be alright.”

But Mydei shook his head. “Leonnius’ whole strength is in his legs! If he ends up not being able to use them after this…”

“Don’t start.” Phainon cupped Mydei’s face with both hands, forcing him to look at him. “If you start down the ‘what ifs,’ you’ll spiral, and that helps no one. Not Leonnius, and not you.”

“You say that, but Leonnius’ efforts were completely in vain!” Mydei’s voice cracked. “It wasn’t even the ring, just some worthless junk shining underwater! How am I supposed to face him if he loses his leg because of that?”

Phainon’s own chest ached, but he held on tighter. He had promised Mydei he’d be his anchor when the time came.

“Mydei… listen to me.” Phainon tried to keep his voice steady. “You’ll make yourself sick if you keep worrying. Leonnius would never blame you for what happened, and neither should you. All we can do now is be strong for him. Be there when he wakes up, no matter the outcome. Later, you can scream, cry, or break down, and I’ll be right here with you. But right now, I need you to stay calm.”

Phainon pressed their foreheads together.

“Thank you…” Mydei whispered. He let himself collapse against his boyfriend.

Phainon held him close, silently offering him comfort. He thought Mydei would go quiet, but he spoke up again.

“I missed you.”

Phainon wanted to hug him, squeeze him tightly and kiss him all over his face. He had missed him terribly too. Instead, he reached for the soap, lathering it before beginning to scrub his hair.

“I missed you too.” He ended up saying when his voice allowed him to.

They sat in the bath quietly. Phainon shifted behind Mydei, so he could rinse and wash his hair properly. That’s when he noticed how much it had grown since the first time they met. It used to barely reach his shoulder, now it went way past it, extending to his back.

“It’s getting long. Maybe I should cut it,” Mydei said, catching on to Phainon’s stare.

“I like it this long. It suits you.”

Once they were done bathing, and Mydei felt his strength coming back, they stepped out and got dressed, taking the time to properly dry their hair until it was no longer dripping.

“Let’s go to the infirmary,” Mydei suggested, wanting to put his mind at ease.

They headed to the infirmary together, and Phainon expected the worst. All kinds of dark scenarios rushed through his mind, each one heavier than the last, but he forced himself to keep his worry hidden from his boyfriend.

As soon as they entered, they were relieved to hear Leonnius was awake, his loud complaining could be heard through the entrance before they even saw him.

“Ouch! Perdikkas, easy on my leg!” he whined.

When he finally came into view, Leonnius was laying on clean sheets, the pile of bloodied ones were balled up at the side of the room. Perdikkas stood at the foot of the bed, wrapping bandages around Leonnius’ injured leg. His eyes were swollen and red, like he had been crying, but at the moment he looked mad.

“Shut up. I just saved your life. You can handle it,” He said coldly, his voice rough from crying.

Leonnius pouted, sinking further into the sheets. “You don’t have to be so mean about it…” he muttered.

“Mean?” Perdikkas snapped, tightening the bandage a little too firmly on purpose. “You nearly bled out in my arms, and I had to stitch you back together. Forgive me if I’m not in the mood for your whining.”

Peucesta, sitting nearby with his arms crossed, finally spoke up. “He’s alive, Perdikkas. That’s what matters. Ease up a little.”

Perdikkas didn’t reply, jaw clenched as he tied off the last bandage with more force than necessary.

Leonnius finally noticed Mydei and Phainon and tried to lighten the mood with a smile. “Hey, Phainon! Haven’t seen you in a while!”

Mydei walked closer to the bed, glancing at Perdikkas as he washed his hands, then turned his attention back to Leonnius.

“How is your leg?”

“It’s all good! I’ll need to take it easy and train it to work properly again, but it should be fine eventually,” Leonnius explained.

Mydei’s fists clenched. That probably meant Leonnius would lose all the strength he’d spent years building in his legs, only to start over.

“Leonnius… I’m sorry. If only I-” Mydei began, but Leonnius cut him off.

“Don’t you dare. That wasn’t your fault. If I had followed proper procedure, this wouldn’t have happened.”

“But I should’ve stopped you,” Mydei tried to argue, but Leonnius left him no room.

“What’s done is done. I don’t blame anyone but myself for what happened. I’m alive now, and that’s all that matters. I don’t want you feeling bad for me, that’s not like you.”

Mydei nodded, reluctantly agreeing. “You’re right…”

“Besides, I’m gonna get a cool scar from this!” Leonnius laughed. “Phainon, you should’ve seen that monster! It was huge, and had these purple scales! And its mouth was bigger than me and had so many rows of teeth!”

“I’m sure that was scary,” Phainon said, though something gnawed at him. The description of that monster… it felt familiar. He had a sudden realization that nobody else seemed to share. Maybe he was mistaken, but he couldn’t shake the feeling.

Leonnius tried hiding a yawn, but it didn’t escape Perdikkas’ sharp eyes.

“Alright, everyone out. Leonnius needs to rest,” Perdikkas ordered, folding his arms across his chest.

“I’m not that tired,” Leonnius protested, though his half lidded eyes betrayed him.

“You shut up. I don’t even know how you’re still conscious after all the blood you lost,” Perdikkas snapped, his eyes softer than his tone.

Everyone left, giving Leonnius the privacy he needed to rest. Phainon followed Mydei back to their room, slipping into bed to cuddle and comfort him. He was grateful for the silence, though his mind was already drifting elsewhere.

Before he knew it, he heard Mydei’s light snores. Phainon chuckled, pressing a kiss to his forehead, relieved to finally have him back in his arms.

The next day, Phainon woke up to find Mydei wasn’t in bed. He was already up, getting dressed.

“Mydei…” Phainon whined, opening his arms.

“Did I wake you?” Mydei leaned closer, hovering over his boyfriend. “I need to give my mother a report about the expedition.”

“Hmm…” Phainon hummed, pulling Mydei into a hug. “You’re finally back and I don’t even get morning cuddles…”

Mydei chuckled, pressing a soft kiss to his boyfriend’s lips. “I’ll clear my morning tomorrow.”

And with that, the prince was gone, leaving Phainon alone in bed. Soon enough, he was up and dressed, finding himself in the library, not to study Kremnoan this time, but with another purpose entirely.

“Where is it…” He muttered under his breath as he scanned the shelves.

“What are you looking for?” A voice asked from the other side of the shelf.

Phainon circled around and found Ptolemy holding a book in his hands.

“Ptolemy! I was looking for a book about…” That’s when his eyes locked on the cover in Ptolemy’s hand. It was exactly what he had been searching for. “…river monsters.”

“You too?” Ptolemy asked, raising a brow.

“You noticed it too?” Phainon asked, hopeful.

“Yeah… something was off about that story.” Ptolemy said, motioning for him to follow. He led Phainon to a table, setting the book down and flipping through the pages.

Phainon watched closely until they found the page they were looking for. He tapped the page lightly. “I’ve heard the legends before, and it even says it here. This monster isn’t aggressive. It’s said to be peaceful, only attacking if it senses danger.”

Ptolemy frowned, his hand hovering over the text. “Then why did it attack Leonnius? Things aren’t adding up.”

They both stayed silent, trying to come up with an explanation, but things didn’t make sense.

“I’ll look more into it. There has to be other books about this monster somewhere around here,” Ptolemy said, breaking the silence.

Before Phainon could respond, footsteps could be heard getting closer. Perdikkas walked in, from behind a shelf where he had been listening in.

“Don’t bother,” he said, crossing his arms. “It’s pointless to keep researching. The expedition has been cancelled.”

Phainon looked confused. “Cancelled? Just like that?”

“Yes. The ring is gone. Most likely swallowed by that monster. And even if it wasn’t, the risk is too great.” Perdikkas explained, probably repeating what was said during Mydei’s meeting with the queen.

Ptolemy frowned. “So we’re just giving up?”

“There’s nothing left to find,” Perdikkas said. “At least, that’s what they think.”

“What do you mean?” Phainon asked.

“That monster is massive. With the structure of its mouth, Leonnius could’ve easily lost his whole leg.”

Ptolemy seemed to understand where he was getting at, but he had to make sure. “What are you trying to say?”

“I’m saying it wasn’t attacking to kill. It was trying to scare them off,” Perdikkas explained.

The gears in Phainon’s head finally began turning. “That has to be it! We should tell Mydei about this discovery!”

“No!” both generals said in unison.

“Mydei wouldn’t go against his mother’s wishes. If we tell him, it’ll only make him yearn to go back without being able to.” Ptolemy said.

“If we want to do something about it, we’ll have to go behind his back.” Perdikkas added.

“I… don’t know how I feel about keeping secrets from Mydei…” Phainon admitted, a strange twist forming in his gut.

“You won’t be keeping secrets. Just… conveniently not mentioning our plan,” Perdikkas said, and Ptolemy nodded in agreement. “Just think about how happy he’ll be when he finds out you found the signet ring.”

It didn’t make Phainon feel any better about the whole thing, but he knew he would have to handle it if he wanted to do something about the situation. “Fine… but we have to be completely ready before we go.”

Over the next week, the three of them kept busy researching, preparing supplies without raising suspicion, and training. Normally, the generals would feel uneasy setting out on such a dangerous journey without Mydei, but since Phainon was just as strong, they placed their trust in him without hesitation.

The night before the expedition, Phainon and Mydei went to their usual training grounds, but instead of sparring, they sat leaning against a pillar they had accidentally broken the other day. From this spot, they could see the stars clearly, away from everyone else.

Phainon wondered why Mydei was acting more romantic than usual today, cornering him twice earlier that day just to make out in not-so-secluded places. Normally, he wouldn’t complain, but the thought gnawed at him. Did Mydei know about tomorrow’s secret expedition?

At that moment, Mydei nuzzled into his neck, trailing kisses along his skin before letting his teeth graze him.

“Mydei…”

“Shush. You’re leaving with Perdikkas to gather herbs for a few days, so I need to make up for it.”

Right… the convenient lie they had told Mydei so they could sneak off to the river of souls. The guilt was unbearable, but Phainon swallowed it down.

“Is that why you’ve failed to keep your hands off me all day?”

“Partly,” Mydei admitted before biting down on his neck hard enough to leave a mark, in a spot visible for all to see. “Did you know you talk in your sleep?”

Phainon’s blood ran cold. He did talk in his sleep sometimes, especially when he was stressed. Could he have revealed their real plan for tomorrow?

“Really? What did I say…?”

Mydei hummed against his skin, kissing the bruise he had just left. “You were counting.”

“Counting?”

“Yeah… one, two, three, four…” Mydei said, switching to Kremnoan.

It suddenly dawned on Phainon, he had given away his other secret. “You weren’t supposed to find out…” he admitted, face heating.

Mydei smiled fondly. “You’ve been learning Kremnoan behind my back?”

“I wanted to surprise you…” Phainon muttered.

“Well, you’ve surprised me.”

“It was supposed to be romantic… not me counting numbers in my sleep.” Phainon groaned, burying his face in his hands.

Mydei chuckled and pried his hands away, pressing their foreheads together. “Like what?”

Phainon hesitated, his heart racing. He wasn’t sure his pronunciation would be any good, he had just learned these words, and he wasn’t confident in his accent yet. But he swallowed the doubt and whispered in Kremnoan. “I love you.”

Mydei’s eyes widened, the shock quickly vanishing. After a moment, he leaned in, his lips brushing against Phainon’s.

“I love you too,” he whispered, before kissing him hungrily.

Without wasting time, Mydei shifted, straddling Phainon’s lap. He didn’t care if anyone stumbled across them. At this moment, all he wanted was him. Who knew discovering that his boyfriend had learned Kremnoan just for him would turn him on so much?

Phainon’s hands instinctively gripped his waist, pulling him closer. Yet, the sweetness of the kiss didn’t prevent the guilt from aching in his heart.

Chapter End Notes

I hope you enjoyed the chapter! It wasn’t too focused on Phaidei but I had to build a plot there. More Phaidei will come next chapter!
As always thank you for reading! Your support and comments are very much appreciated!

chapters.title: Chapter 3
chapters.html:
Chapter Notes

I promise I didn’t forget about this fic! I got distracted by another ship and used the opportunity to write something out of my comfort zone. I also had a thesis to work on and patients reports to write so I didn’t want to rush this chapter. I finally had the time to write so I humbly offer you the final chapter! Enjoy!

See the end of the chapter for more notes

Safe to say, Phainon did not get any sleep that night. If it had been any other night, he would’ve been overjoyed to know how much it meant to Mydei that he had learned Kremnoan for him. But with the early departure looming, the timing couldn’t have been worse.

When he finally drifted off, it was barely for two hours. His body was sore and exhausted, but he forced himself to move, knowing he had to get up.

The moment he shifted, he was stopped by the weight of Mydei’s arms tightening around him. The prince’s head rested against his chest, his grip on Phainon’s waist firm, not letting go.

Phainon froze, his heart aching. He brushed a hand over Mydei’s hair, careful not to wake him, and whispered, “I’m sorry…”

He began easing Mydei’s arm off his waist, moving slowly to not wake him up. Mydei sighed in his sleep, tightening his hold for a moment before finally loosening just enough. Phainon slipped free, replacing his body with a pillow before getting dressed. Once he was done, he returned to the bedside, leaning down to press a kiss to Mydei’s forehead.

“I’ll be back…” he whispered.

Phainon walked toward the infirmary, where they had agreed to meet. In the silence of the early morning, faint voices carried clearly. The closer he got, the more he could make out the conversation between Perdikkas and Leonnius.

“…and the balm should last you until I come back. Don’t be reckless.”

“I should be telling you that.”

“Don’t start. You weren’t even supposed to be awake.”

“Oh please. I know you were being loud on purpose, just so I’d wake up and see you off.”

“Not everything is about you.” Perdikkas snapped.

Phainon slowed his steps, hesitating by the door. Are they… arguing? Should he wait for Ptolemy to get here before he enters?

“You’d be bored to death without me.” Leonnius said smugly.

“I’d be less stressed without you.” Perdikkas replied.

“Don’t pretend you don’t like it when I push your buttons. You’d miss me.” Leonnius teased.

“Shut up.”

“Make me-”

Suddenly, everything went silent. Phainon was worried, he got closer to the door and peeked inside, only to instantly regret it.

Leonnius was leaning against the counter, arms hooked around Perdikkas’ neck as they made out. He was smirking into the kiss, enjoying the result of his actions.

Phainon had seen enough. He looked away immediately, face burning. So this is how everyone else feels when they walk in on him and Mydei being handsy?

Before he could retreat, he heard footsteps getting closer. Phainon froze when he saw Ptolemy. He made movements with his arms, crossing them, signaling him not to enter.

But Ptolemy walked right in. “Perdikkas we’re here-” he stopped dead in his tracks, staring at them.

Perdikkas and Leonnius broke apart instantly, Leonnius still grinning, satisfied with himself, while Perdikkas looked like he wanted the floor to swallow him whole.

Ptolemy sighed, rubbing his forehead. “Seriously? This is how you prepare?”

Leonnius chuckled. “I’m giving him stress-relief.”

Perdikkas groaned, turning away, busying himself with supplies. “We’re leaving. Now.”

Soon they were out of the infirmary, awkward silence lingering between them. That didn’t last long, due to Phainon’s talkative nature.

“How long is it going to take to get there?”

“It should only take about two days. Getting to the Sea of Souls isn’t the part that will take the most time,” Perdikkas explained.

“We’re going to need to discuss fighting strategy. I studied that monster’s movements from what the others described and from the little literature I could find,” Ptolemy said. “We’ll go over it when we set camp for the night.”

With that, they walked mostly in silence, taking breaks here and there to discuss what needed to be done. At night, they took turns keeping watch. Ptolemy first, being used to late-night reading, Perdikkas in the middle of the night, and Phainon, who always woke up early, taking the final shift.

Before long, they reached the Sea of Souls. As expected, monsters attacked as soon as they stepped in, but fighting them was no issue. Luckily, Ptolemy’s research paid off, he guided them through several paths that were clear of danger.

Eventually, they set up camp for the last time before reaching the sea monster’s lair. Phainon was supposed to be asleep, but no matter how much he tossed and turned, rest wouldn’t come.

“Getting nervous?” Ptolemy asked.

“Yeah…” Phainon admitted.

“If we stick to the plan, we should make it out alive.”

“I know… I just hope we’ll actually find the signet ring.” Phainon sighed, sitting up.

“And if we don’t?”

Phainon buried his face in his hands. “I lied to Mydei for this… if I come back empty-handed, I think he might divorce me…”

“You aren’t even married yet and you’re already scared of divorce?” Ptolemy chuckled.

“You know what I mean!” Phainon pouted.

“You talk like Mydei would stop loving you over that.”

Phainon hesitated. Mydei wouldn’t stop loving him, but the trust they shared would be shattered. It could ruin everything.

“Stop worrying. Everything will be fine. Now go to sleep before I knock you out unconscious.” Ptolemy smirked, leaning back against his pack.

The next morning, Phainon woke the others. They packed their belongings and readied themselves. The path ahead would lead them directly to the sea monster’s lair. From what Leonnius and the others had told them, the road would be narrow, the water overtaking most of the land. They’d have minimal space to fight and more blind spots for the monster to surge from.

The plan was for Phainon to fight it off, since he was the strongest, while the other two searched the area for the reason behind the attacks. This monster was known to be peaceful, so there had to be something agitating it.

As expected, they reached the narrow path. Phainon walked at the back, keeping an eye on their blind spots. One mistake could mean their deaths. But no matter how far they went, the monster didn’t show. Phainon tossed a stick into the water, hoping to provoke it, but nothing happened.

“Something’s wrong… we passed the spot where Mydei’s group was attacked. We should’ve seen it by now.” Ptolemy said.

That’s when they heard a banging noise. Once, twice, then a roar. Somehow, it sounded sad.

Perdikkas, walking ahead, motioned for them to stay quiet. As they approached, they saw on the other side of the river, the giant monster struggling to lift massive rocks with its head. The round shapes and slippery scales kept it from moving the stones no matter how hard it tried.

Phainon’s mind was racing. The monster was strong enough to crush rocks if it wanted. Why was it trying to lift them? Was something fragile trapped underneath? The cracks in the cliff above suggested the rocks had fallen recently. Without thinking, he stepped onto the river stones, crossing as quickly as he could.

“Phainon, don’t-!” Perdikkas called, but it was too late.

Phainon reached the other side and approached the monster. It roared the instant it saw him, ready to strike. But Phainon didn’t draw his sword. He raised his hands instead.

“I’m here to help!” he shouted, hoping the creature would understand his body language if not his words.

The monster stilled, watching him carefully. Phainon took that as permission to move. He walked closer to the pile of rocks and peered underneath, only to freeze when the monster roared again.

Now he understood.

Beneath the rocks lay broken eggshells, and three baby sea monsters. One was pinned under a stone, while the other two clawed helplessly at the opening, unable to squeeze through.

Phainon looked up at the creature again. “We’ll help you,” he said before waving his friends over, who were already in the process of crossing the river.

“The monster’s babies are trapped under the rocks. We need to free them,” Phainon explained quickly.

Perdikkas crouched down, examining the situation. “The two that are free will be easy to pull out. But the one pinned under that stone… we’ll need to be careful if we want it alive.”

They began with the smaller task first, removing the loose stones at the top to widen the opening. Bit by bit, they managed to pull out the two uninjured babies. The mother immediately circled around them, nudging each one, as though checking to make sure they were unharmed.

Then came the real challenge. The last baby was crushed under a boulder too large to be moved by hand. Phainon pressed his palms under it and strained, but the stone didn’t budge.

“We need leverage,” Ptolemy said, scanning their surroundings. He pointed to a sturdy branch that had drifted near the water’s edge. “If we wedge that under the rock and use another stone as the base, we can make a lever. We just need to lift it enough to release the pressure.”

They hurried to put the plan together. Perdikkas put a flat rock into place while Phainon dragged the heavy branch over. Working together, they jammed the branch under the edge of the boulder.

They heaved with all their strength. The branch bended under the weight, but the boulder shifted just slightly. It was enough. Ptolemy quickly reached in and pulled the trapped baby free.

Perdikkas laid a blanket on the ground, motioning for Ptolemy to set the injured baby down. The little creature was bleeding, and it needed treatment before the wound became infected. He worked carefully, cleaning and bandaging as best he could. For someone with no medical knowledge of sea monsters, he figured he did a decent job.

Once he was finished, Phainon gently handed the baby back to its mother. She immediately gathered her young close, curling around them protectively.

“Now that everything’s settled, we can start looking for the ring.” Phainon announced.

“Yeah… but this place looks deserted,” Perdikkas pointed out, scanning the barren rocks and riverbank.

That’s when an idea struck Phainon. He dug through their supplies until he pulled out the sketch of the signet ring that Ptolemy had drawn. Holding it up, he showed it to the massive creature.

“Have you seen this?” he asked, not sure she would understand.

To his surprise, the sea monster let out a roar and slipped beneath the water. A minute passed and she resurfaced, carrying a dripping mess of tangled jewelry in her jaws. She dropped the glittering pile at their feet, golden chains and jeweled rings clattering against the stones.

“Wow! That’s enough gold to last us a lifetime,” Ptolemy said, crouching eagerly beside the treasure.

Phainon sifted through the wet tangle of necklaces, earrings, and rings until his eye caught it.

“There it is! The signet ring!”

He held it close, examining it, hardly believing it was real. The long journey, the dangers, the guilt had all been worth it.

Or at least, that’s what he thought.

Because far away, a certain crown prince had already discovered the truth and was waiting, furious, for Phainon’s return.

The journey back to Castrum Kremnos felt longer than it was. Phainon carried the signet ring close to his chest, refusing to let it leave his sight. He told himself over and over that once he handed it to Mydei, everything would be forgiven.

But the closer they got, the heavier his chest felt. Eventually they made it through the gates at midnight. It was eerily silent. Ptolemy and Perdikkas each went to their rooms to rest. Phainon, on the other hand went to Mydei’s.

As soon as he walked in, he saw his boyfriend standing at the window, back facing him.

“Mydei, I’m back.” Phainon said, expecting a heartfelt welcome.

“You lied to me.” Mydei’s voice was cold, devoid of all emotions.

Phainon’s heart sank to his stomach. “I did…”

“You’d better have a good explanation for your actions.”

Mydei finally turned to face him, and Phainon froze. He’d seen Mydei angry before, but never like this. It was closer to disappointment.

“I wanted to tell you about our plan,” Phainon started, “but you would’ve stopped us from going. The ring means so much to you, and I couldn’t just let you give up on it.”

“Why do you think we stopped searching?” Mydei snapped. “Leonnius could’ve died! You could’ve died too!”

Phainon stepped closer, lowering his voice. “I’m sorry, Mydei… but I’d do it again for you.”

“Hks…” Mydei sighed, shutting his eyes.

“What?” Phainon blinked. It sounded like Kremnoan, but he didn’t know the word.

Mydei opened his eyes again, the anger softening into exhaustion. “I’m not telling you to follow my orders. I just don’t want you to lie to me.”

Phainon reached for his hand. “I can promise you that.” He lifted it and pressed a kiss to his knuckles.

“You’re impossible…” Mydei muttered, shaking his head. “Did you kill the monster, then? I assume you did, since you’re standing here.”

Phainon smiled, chest puffed with pride. “Nope! We helped her rescue her babies. After that, she wasn’t aggressive anymore.”

Mydei stared at him, then let out a chuckle he tried to hold back. “Befriending a monster… I don’t know what I expected.”

Ah. How Phainon had missed that smile.

“You do realize that you, Perdikkas, and Ptolemy will be punished for disobeying the queen’s orders.” Mydei continued once he’d calmed down.

“Seriously? Can’t my lovely prince save me?” Phainon pouted.

“Castrum Kremnos doesn’t officially recognize ‘boyfriends,’ so there’s nothing I can do.” Mydei smirked.

Phainon dropped to one knee, still holding Mydei’s hand. With his free hand, he pulled out the signet ring from his pocket.

“What about fiancés?”

Mydei’s eyes widened for more than one reason. Phainon couldn’t help grinning at the dumbfounded expression. It was rare to catch Mydei off guard, and he was going to enjoy it.

“You… found the ring?” Mydei finally managed.

“The kind mother monster found it for us.” Phainon said, tilting his head. “Now, you didn’t answer my question.”

For a moment, Mydei just stood there, completely still.

“Phainon…” he said in disbelief. “You are absolutely incorrigible.”

“And yet, you love me for it.” Phainon couldn’t remove that stupid smile off his face.

“Unfortunately.” Mydei muttered, though the warmth in his tone betrayed him. He looked down at Phainon again.

“Get up.”

Phainon blinked. “Is that a yes?”

“It’s a get up before I change my mind.” Mydei said, but when Phainon stood, he reached out and cupped his cheek, eyes softening. “Of course it’s a yes, you idiot.”

Phainon instantly smiled widely. “You really said yes?”

“Yes.” Mydei laughed, barely able to get the word out before Phainon lifted him off the ground in a crushing hug.

“Mydeimos, future husband of mine!” Phainon declared proudly, spinning him around.

“Put me down before I revoke my answer!” Mydei yelped, laughing despite himself.

When Phainon finally set him down, he took the ring and slid it onto Mydei’s finger. The fit was perfect.

“I’d cross the sea of souls a hundred times over if it meant I’d get to see you wear it.” Phainon whispered, admiring how the ring looked.

Mydei pulled his now fiancé close and pressed their lips together. No words could express what he wanted to say better than that kiss.

When they finally parted, Mydei sighed against his lips. “You still have to face my mother tomorrow.”

“Worth it,” Phainon murmured, already leaning in for another kiss.

Mydei chuckled, eyes fluttering shut again. Maybe he could distract his mother with wedding preparations long enough to spare Phainon and the others from punishment.

“Mydeimos.” Gorgo sat at her desk, Krateros standing by her side. She had summoned Phainon, Perdikkas, and Ptolemy, yet it was her son standing before her. “I believe I didn’t call for you,” she said.

“I’m aware. They’re waiting outside,” Mydei replied.

“I assume you’ve already spoken with Phainon?” Gorgo’s tone was sharp. She loved her son dearly, but there were matters of discipline she could not overlook.

“Yes,” Mydei said. “And I believe punishment is… unnecessary.”

“Unnecessary?” Krateros repeated, his voice rising with disbelief. “Excuse me, prince, but he disobeyed the queen’s direct orders. We can’t simply let him go free because you fancy him.”

“I have to agree with Krateros,” Gorgo said, studying her son closely. She knew him too well not to sense there was more behind his words. “We can’t give him special treatment just because he’s your boyfriend.”

“Fiancé.”

Krateros blinked, unsure he’d heard correctly. “...Fiancé?”

Gorgo’s brows lifted, her composure slipping for the first time. “I beg your pardon?”

“Phainon proposed. And I said yes.” Mydei explained.

For a moment, neither Gorgo nor Krateros spoke. The queen’s serious expression softened into disbelief. “He disobeyed orders, dragged two generals with him, and he had the audacity to propose?”

“They were the ones who dragged him but yes, he did propose.” Mydei confirmed. “And he brought back the signet ring. The monster wasn’t hostile, it was protecting its young ones. He helped it instead of killing it.”

Gorgo pressed a hand to her forehead, stifling a laugh. “Of course he did.”

“Your Majesty,” Krateros started, still outraged, “this is unacceptable! Disobedience cannot be rewarded with marriage-”

“Oh relax, Krateros.” Gorgo interrupted, waving a hand dismissively. “No one’s rewarding him. I’m simply… prioritizing the wedding over punishment. The signet ring has been returned, no one was injured, and my son’s finally settling down.”

“But-” Krateros started before sighing. He knew there was nothing he could say that would convince the queen.

Phainon sat breathless in the infirmary, chugging down an entire cup of water.

“You’re going to give yourself a side stitch if you drink that much after running,” Perdikkas said, glancing up from where he was examining Leonnius’ leg. After the incident, it was healing surprisingly well. Sure, it left a scar, but that seemed to be the only lasting consequence.

Leonnius had recently been cleared to exercise again, under one condition. No overexertion. To make sure of that, Phainon volunteered to train with him. Every morning, they’d run up and down the hill, and Perdikkas would examine Leonnius afterward.

“Your leg looks fine,” Perdikkas said, straightening up. “You can increase your speed tomorrow, but stop the second you feel something off.”

“You worry too much. I still can’t believe you assigned Phainon as my babysitter.” Leonnius joked, tugging his pant leg back down. “Stealing him away from Mydei’s morning training two weeks before their wedding, no less. How cruel.”

Phainon shook his head with a small smile. “No, I think it’s for the best.”

“I agree.” Perdikkas added dryly. “Those two can’t seem to keep their hands off each other. I guarantee they get more actual training done when they’re separated.”

Leonnius laughed, leaning back on the bed. “He’s got a point, you know. I swear, every time I pass the training grounds, you two are never sparring. You’re always all over each other.”

Phainon’s cheeks reddened instantly. “You’re just jealous I’m getting married before you.”

“Me? Jealous? Not a chance.” Leonnius chuckled, glancing at Perdikkas from the corner of his eye, who was across the room, neatly putting his tools back in place. “Just wait until your wedding’s over,” he murmured quietly, just loud enough for Phainon to hear. “I’ve got plans of my own.”

Phainon’s jaw dropped. He wanted to say something, but with Perdikkas still in the room, his brain completely short-circuited.

“By the way,” Perdikkas said suddenly, appearing right beside them and nearly making Phainon jump out of his seat. “Did you end up proposing in Kremnoan?”

“Oh.” Realization hit Phainon. “I forgot.”

Meanwhile, in Aedes Elysiae, Audata and Hieronymus were in their small garden, tending to their plants. Pomegranate season was approaching, and Phainon had promised to bring Mydei then so he could taste their pomegranate delicacies.

The sun hung high in the sky, signaling it was time for a break. Just then, in the distance, they noticed a pink-haired girl sprinting toward them, clutching an envelope in her hands.

“Cyrene? What brings you here?” Audata asked, wiping the sweat from her forehead.

“I got a letter from Phainon, but it’s addressed to all three of us. I thought we should open it together.” She held up the envelope. It was unlike his usual letters. Red paper, thicker than normal, with golden lines tracing the corners and sealed with a golden wax stamp.

“This looks fancy. Did Phainon raid the stash for official correspondence?” Hieronymus joked as he joined them.

“I wouldn’t put it past him,” Cyrene said with a grin, carefully breaking the seal to avoid damaging it. Her eyes scanned the contents, and then she froze.

“What’s wrong? Did something happen?” Audata asked, sensing the sudden shift in her expression.

Cyrene looked up, her voice somewhere between disbelief and amusement. “Phainon is inviting us to Castrum Kremnos… to attend his wedding.”

Chapter End Notes

I was debating writing the wedding, but I had no idea what culture to inspire the wedding from so I just gave up. You can also clearly tell I’ve been enjoying shipping Leonnius and Perdikkas.
I hope you enjoyed this fic! Phaidei will always have a special place in my heart!
